scope: Bun compilation options, ambient file autoload exclusion, version/commit definitions, target/runtime support
checkout: /tmp/rev44clone (detached at target; /workspace/repo left at assigned baseline 5672ead, clean)

findings.title: buildConfig ignores the `root` argument, so packaging another source tree silently ships this repository's code
findings.evidence: buildConfig hardcodes entrypoints: [join(repositoryRoot, "src", "cli.ts")], while packageVersion (scripts/build.ts:94), repositoryCommit (scripts/build.ts:110) and packageCli (scripts/package.ts:272-286) honour an options.root parameter. Version/commit come from `root`; code always comes from repositoryRoot.
findings.reproduction: Bun 1.4.2, /tmp/probe/root-probe.ts: created /tmp/probe/altroot with package.json version 9.9.9-alt plus one git commit, then called packageCli({ root: "/tmp/probe/altroot", outDir: "/tmp/probe/altdist" }) -> exit 0, produced swarmforge-v9.9.9-alt-linux-x64-glibc.tar.gz and metadata-9.9.9-alt.json with commit f1d7b3d2..., while the archived binary is this repository's src/cli.ts build (82,695,648 bytes; --help prints this repo's usage).
findings.recommendation: Thread root into buildConfig and use join(root, "src", "cli.ts"), or remove the root parameter so the mismatch cannot be expressed.
findings.guard_gap: packageCli's executable.version !== version check (scripts/package.ts:287) compares two values derived from the same root, so it is self-consistent; verifyArchive only cross-checks define'd strings, the digest and the executable's own --version/--help. No test or CLI path passes root, so impact is latent rather than live in CI.

findings.title: SHA256SUMS covers only the executable, leaving the shipped version/commit metadata unverified by the documented install step
findings.evidence: checksums() emits one line for the executable only; README.md:50-52 teaches `sha256sum -c SHA256SUMS` as the operator's verification of the downloaded archive.
findings.reproduction: Code-evidenced: a repacked archive whose metadata-<version>.json was edited passes `sha256sum -c` because the manifest never covers that file. Not executed (would require building a tampered archive).
findings.recommendation: Add a manifest line for the metadata file and extend verifyArchive's expectedFiles and checksum expectations accordingly.
findings.guard_gap: verifyArchive validates metadata against the executable inside the same archive, so nothing binds the metadata bytes to the shipped digest; CI catches a repack, the operator-facing post-download check does not.

findings.title: Build provenance ignores a dirty worktree, so a modified checkout is stamped with a clean HEAD commit
findings.evidence: repositoryCommit() validates only that `git -C root rev-parse HEAD` exits 0 and yields 40 hex chars; no `git status --porcelain` check exists in scripts/build.ts, scripts/package.ts or the release workflow.
findings.reproduction: Code-evidenced (not executed in CI, where checkouts are clean): running `bun run build` from a checkout with uncommitted edits records HEAD, which does not describe the shipped source; the workflow cross-check `--help | grep "build $(git rev-parse HEAD)"` compares against the same HEAD and would also pass.
findings.recommendation: Check worktree cleanliness before compiling and either refuse to package a dirty tree or record a dirty flag in the metadata; enforce it inside packageCli so all callers get it.
findings.guard_gap: No cleanliness guard exists; scripts/build.ts:104-107 documents the commit as the operator's mapping back to source, which a dirty build silently invalidates.

findings.title: Duplicated, unused advertisedPlatform constant in scripts/build.ts invites silent drift
findings.evidence: scripts/build.ts:25 exports advertisedPlatform = "linux-x64-glibc" with no importer anywhere (grep over src/tests/scripts); the live copy is scripts/package.ts:40, used by archiveName (scripts/package.ts:67) and buildMetadata (scripts/package.ts:97).
findings.reproduction: Code-evidenced: editing scripts/build.ts:25 changes no archive name, metadata field or test outcome; tests/packaging.test.ts asserts compileTarget but not the platform literal.
findings.recommendation: Delete the dead export in scripts/build.ts or have scripts/package.ts import it from a single source.
findings.guard_gap: No test binds the archive name or metadata platform to a single definition, so a change applied to the wrong copy passes CI.

verified_correct: autoloadDotenv/autoloadBunfig are the only live defaults (node_modules/bun-types/bun.d.ts:3684-3714 documents them @default true; autoloadTsconfig/autoloadPackageJson already default false), and all four keys are real Bun 1.4.2 API members. A binary compiled from target ignored a foreign .env (source: default) while a control binary compiled without the flags read it (source: env), proving the flags work; it also ignored .env/bunfig.toml placed beside the executable.
Source-run suppression verified: `bun --no-env-file --config=/dev/null src/cli.ts config show` ignored the foreign .env while a bare source run read it.

Version/commit defines verified: `bun scripts/build.ts` reported version 0.1.0 and commit d428e0f730ed5649485732e95d39c32f5d6a8895; a control build reported 9.9.9 / build cafecafe..., confirming define substitution covers the typeof guards at src/version.ts:29 and src/version.ts:43.

Target/runtime support honest: bun-linux-x64-baseline is a valid CompileTarget; the binary is ELF x86-64 dynamically linked to glibc with maximum required symbol version GLIBC_2.17 (objdump -T), matching advertisedPlatform linux-x64-glibc; bytecode:false produces plain transpiled JS as documented.
